title: Open-circuit option for closed topologies (toroid/poloidal/Rodin) — break the loop so tips source C
description:
Closed windings (toroid, toroid_poloidal, rodin) have ∇·J≈0 everywhere → ∂µJµ≈0 → no EED scalar C → no Φ_g, regardless of winding cleverness. The open helix works precisely because its wire does NOT close: free tips → charge accumulates under AC → ∇·J≠0 → sources C. (open_helix is literally the same path as solenoid; openness is the whole mechanism.)

FEATURE: an open_circuit flag (CoilParams) that breaks a closed winding so it has free tips, applicable to any topology. When on:
- biot/builders.rs: truncate the trailing ~8% of the path for closed types (Toroid/ToroidPoloidal/Rodin) → two separated tips. Already-open types (solenoid/open_helix/flat_spiral) unchanged.
- Drive: AC current (existing current_a + frequency_hz). The open path + AC → ∇·J≠0 at tips → C. Backend is_ac_current_source already routes any current type with freq>0 through AC injection.
- Frontend: open_circuit toggle (current-carrying, non-capacitor/mass types); expose the frequency slider whenever open_circuit is on (so the user can AC-drive it); default a frequency when enabling.

Test: open toroid (AC) sources C >> closed toroid. Lets the user compare which OPEN topology concentrates Φ_g most — the actual experiment-design question.
notes:
FOLLOW-UP 2 (open circuits are voltage-driven): an open circuit is antenna-like — you can't force a defined current through free tips; you apply a voltage and I follows from the impedance (same reason open_helix is voltage-driven). Made it consistent:
- builders.rs entity_to_segments + lib.rs AC path: voltage-driven (I₀=V₀/OPEN_HELIX_Z_REF=V₀/50Ω) for OpenHelix OR any coil with open_circuit set; closed loops still use current_a.
- AC warning generalized '(open helix)' → '(open circuit)'.
- Frontend: isVoltageDriven = open_helix || (canOpen && isOpen); shows the Voltage V₀ slider (max 50 kV) instead of Current for open coils; the open-circuit toggle pre-fills 2500 V (→50 A) alongside the 1 GHz frequency.
- Test: open case now drives voltage_v=2500 (=50 A), matching the closed current_a=50 — identical result (open 1.5964e-3, 2.9×), confirming the V/Z conversion is equivalent.
Full suite 24 ok/0 fail; tsc clean.

title: κ_G=1 toroid sanity diagnostic
description:
Quick (~30s) diagnostic before any code change.

## What
Run a toroidal coil in time-domain FDTD with κ_G = 1.0 (unphysical, but isolates the coupling form from the magnitude problem). Check the Φ_g and B_g_magnitude slices and maxima.

## Expected outcome
Still zero / floating-point noise — because the current coupling channel (κ_G·∂C/∂t for Φ_g, κ_G·∇C for A_g) is structurally blind to a static toroidal A-field where C is near-constant and ∂C/∂t = 0.

## Why this matters
This confirms the diagnosis in the conversation thread before we change the physics. If by some chance Φ_g lights up at κ_G=1, the problem is purely precision (just do bead 3 — rescale) and we can leave the coupling form alone. If it stays zero, beads 2/4/5 are all required.

## How to apply
- entities: 1 × CoilType::Toroid, current_a = 10, frequency_hz = 0
- gem: enabled=true, kappa_g = 1.0, li_torr_mode = false
- solver: TimeDomain { dt_s = 0.0, n_steps = 200 }
- Inspect: PhiG slice on Z=0.5, BgMagnitude max value

Report findings in this issue's notes before opening ORC-2 (direct coupling).
notes:

## Setup
New reproducible test: solver-gpu/tests/gem_kappa_diagnostic.rs
- 1× Toroid, radius 0.05 m, 20 turns, current_a=10, frequency_hz=0 (DC/static)
- gem: enabled=true, kappa_g=1.0 (unphysical, isolates form from magnitude), li_torr_mode=false
- solver: TimeDomain { dt_s=0.0 (auto CFL), n_steps=200 }, 32³ grid, domain_radius 0.10 m
- Inspected Z=0.5 slice peaks for B, C, Φ_g, B_g + global maxima.

## Result (cargo test --test gem_kappa_diagnostic -- --nocapture)
  |B|   peak = 1.2177e-3 T      ← EM field present, Biot-Savart works
  |C|   peak = 0.0000e0  1/m    ← C≈0 on midplane (Coulomb-gauge Biot-Savart)
  Φ_g   peak = 0.0000e0  m²/s²  ← gravitational scalar DARK
  |B_g| peak = 0.0000e0  1/s    ← gravitomagnetic DARK
  |B_g|/|B| = 0.000e0
Test passes (asserts |B_g|/|B| < 1e-3).

## Interpretation
Even at the absurd κ_G=1, Φ_g and B_g stay at exactly zero. The DC toroid is a
static magnetic config: A is time-independent ⇒ ∂C/∂t = 0, and C = ∇·A ≈ 0
(Coulomb gauge) ⇒ ∇C ≈ 0. Both κ_G source channels (κ_G·∂C/∂t → Φ_g,
κ_G·∇C → A_g) vanish. Structural confirmation reinforced by the code path:
run_gem_fdtd snapshots c_fld_prev once from the post-EM-loop c_fld, so the GEM
solver sees ∂C/∂t≈0 throughout.

## Conclusion
The derivative coupling form is STRUCTURALLY BLIND to static configurations —
NOT a precision problem. Therefore:
  • ORC-bn6 (direct KK coupling Φ_g←κ_G·C, A_g←κ_G·A) IS required.
  • ORC-j07 (interleave EM/GEM, per-step ∂C/∂t) and ORC-0tl (ρ_m/J_m sources)
    remain required.
  • The precision-only escape hatch (rescale-only, ORC-gru in isolation) is
    ruled OUT — rescale alone would still source from zero.
Unblocks ORC-bn6.

title: Wire ρ_m and J_m mass-current GEM sources
description:
## Missing physics
The standard GEM Maxwell-analog sources are not implemented (shader comment explicitly notes \"add in Phase 5\"):
- Φ_g equation lacks `4πG·ρ_m`
- A_g equation lacks `(4πG/c)·J_m`

Without these, the only source path to GEM is the EED→GEM coupling (the κ_G channel), which means **gravitational sourcing from ordinary mass distributions and currents has no representation at all**.

## Why this matters
1. Required for Woodward effect testbed (Wilhelm 2026 Eq. 24: δm(t) ∝ ∂²E/∂t² / Φ_g requires a background Φ_g sourced by ρ_m).
2. Required for Mach-effect thruster predictions.
3. Provides the GEM-only baseline against which EED-coupled effects can be measured.

## Fix
1. Add a `MassEntity` type — a region with `density_kg_m3` (constant or function of position) and an optional `velocity_m_s` (uniform translation for J_m, or `angular_velocity` for rotation).
2. Alternatively: add `mass_density_kg_m3` and `mass_velocity_m_s` fields to existing CoilEntity, gated by a `mass_source: bool` flag — useful for \"this current is carried by Cooper pairs with effective m_e/e ratio\" scenarios.
3. New shader `gem_mass_source.wgsl`: at every vertex inside a mass entity, add `4πG·ρ_m` to `phi_g_vel` per step and `(4πG/c)·ρ_m·v` to `a_g_vel` per component.
4. Constant: 4πG ≈ 8.385×10⁻¹⁰ — survives f32 directly.
5. UI: mass entity card in the geometry panel; visualize Φ_g ≈ Newtonian potential inside/around the entity.

## Validation
Uniform sphere of mass M radius R: outside, Φ_g should match −G·M/r within 1% on a 128³ grid.

## Depends on
ORC-5 (Li-Torr) — shares angular-velocity field infrastructure and \"entity-internal source kernel\" pattern.

DONE (static core + UI + validation; dynamic per-step source split to a P3 follow-up).

PHYSICS (convention resolved with user — gravity attracts, +4πG):
- Static/elliptic (shipped): ∇²Φ_g=4πG·ρ_m, ∇²A_g=(4πG/c²)·J_m (J_m=ρ_m·v). RHS carries NO c² (Poisson directly) → Φ_g=−GM/r. The bead's '4πG·ρ_m' is right for THIS path; the bead's '+ to phi_g_vel per step' would be the time-domain leapfrog, which needs −4πG·c²·ρ_m (c² cancels the wave operator). - state.rs: MassSourceGpu struct + run_gem_mass_static — samples ρ_m/J_m on the grid, solves via run_cg_phi (additive: reads existing Φ_g/A_g and superposes), correct attractive sign.
- lib.rs Phase 4: builds mass sources from entities with ρ_m>0, runs run_gem_mass_static before run_derive_gem_fields (so B_g picks up mass A_g). Independent of κ_G; runs even at κ_G=0.

VALIDATION (tests/gem_mass_newtonian.rs): static MassSphere, two-point 1/r fit cancels the Dirichlet-BC offset → GM_est=4.126e-6 vs GM_true=4.368e-6 = 5.5% on 64³; Φ_g<0 (attractive) and monotonically deepening. Full suite 19 ok/0 fail; tsc clean.

title: Spurious 'AC current=0' warning for voltage-driven capacitors (stale frequency flips has_ac)
description:
Repro: select a TTB/symmetric capacitor in time-domain mode after a coil type that had frequency_hz>0. The leftover frequency_hz (capacitors show no frequency slider) makes the global has_ac flag true (lib.rs:140 = any e.frequency_hz>0, no type filter). The has_ac block then routes the voltage-driven capacitor through the AC *current*-injection path, computes current_a=0 (capacitor → _ => current_a = 0), and warns 'AC injection: f=...Hz but effective current = 0 A — Set Voltage>0 (open helix) or Current>0 A'. Nonsensical: a capacitor is voltage-driven (V=50kV is set), has no current slider, and the FDTD has no AC voltage-modulation path for capacitors anyway.

(AC voltage-modulated capacitors — Biefeld-Brown AC — are a separate unimplemented feature; out of scope here.)

title: GEM FDTD has the ORC-4eg instability: fused skew vel + spurious c² on ∇(∂Φ_g/∂t) → NaN under any live drive
description:
Discovered while validating ORC-j07 (interleaved SLW-GEM). fdtd_gem.wgsl vel_gem replicates every bug ORC-4eg fixed in the EM sector:

1. FUSED skew velocity read: vel_gem updates phi_g_vel using div(a_g_vel@n) AND a_g_vel using ∇(phi_g_vel@n) — both read OLD velocities → longitudinal sub-update [[1,−iβ],[−iβ,1]], |λ|=√(1+β²)>1, unconditionally unstable.
2. SPURIOUS c² on the gradient cross-term: A_g-eq has C2*(lap_agx − gpgv_x), i.e. c²·∇(∂Φ_g/∂t). Per the blessed EED form the temporal cross term carries NO c² (β≈5e8 at CFL otherwise).

Latent until now because run_gem_fdtd only ever ran on STATIC/dark configs (∂C/∂t≈0, ∇C≈0 — nothing to amplify). ORC-j07 interleaved it under an AC open-helix drive with a real ∂C/∂t, and it blew up: phi_g 29791/35937 (83%) non-finite, b_g 100905/143748 (70%) non-finite. The ORC-fwe max-reduction NaN-masking reported the blowup as EXACTLY 0 (Φ_g=0, B_g=0), which is how it stayed hidden.

FIX (mirror ORC-4eg): split vel_gem → vel_gem_phi (writes phi_g_vel) then vel_gem_a (reads the FRESH phi_g_vel for ∇(∂Φ_g/∂t)); drop the c² on that gradient term; keep 0.5·CFL (already inherited from EM dt). Keep the longitudinal-propagating c²∇²A_g form (no −c²∇(∇·A_g)) per FIELD_THEORY.md 2026-05-29. Update GemStepper + run_gem_fdtd to dispatch 3 passes. Re-validate gem_slw_interleaved stays finite and non-zero.

2. Dropped spurious c² on the gradient cross-term: C2*(lap_ag − gpgv) → C2*lap_ag − gpgv.

title: AC voltage modulation for capacitors (Biefeld-Brown drive) — oscillate plate φ so the TTB sources C/Φ_g
description:
Capacitors are static-φ: initialize_phi_capacitor sets the plate field once, no current, no time-variation. So C = ∇·A + (1/c²)∂φ/∂t = 0 → Φ_g = 0 regardless of voltage. The TTB/Biefeld-Brown effect is a HIGH-VOLTAGE AC phenomenon, so to make the capacitor source the EED scalar we need to modulate the plate potential in time:

  φ_plates(t) = ±(V/2)·sin(2π·f·t)   each FDTD step

giving ∂φ/∂t ≠ 0 → C ≠ 0 → Φ_g. 

IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH:
- A capacitor-φ-injection pass analogous to inject_j: re-impose the (asymmetric) plate φ scaled by sin(ωt) each step (or a φ-velocity source), so ∂φ/∂t is sustained AC rather than a one-shot static IC.
- Make capacitor types AC-capable (expose frequency; has_ac/is_ac_* currently excludes them as non-current sources — add a separate 'is_ac_voltage_source' path).
- For the TTB asymmetric capacitor the φ is non-uniform (point electrode), so ∂φ/∂t and ∇C are asymmetric → directional Φ_g (the canonical TTB thrust-direction claim).
- Snapshot timing: sustained AC → post-FDTD snapshot (ORC-x7m), like the open helix.
- Validate: AC TTB capacitor sources C>0 and an asymmetric Φ_g; DC capacitor stays Φ_g≈0.

Context: user raised the capacitor voltage slider to 200 kV to explore the TTB, but DC voltage alone can't produce Φ_g — this is the missing piece.

DIRECTIONALITY MEASURED (tests/gem_ttb_directional.rs): sampling |Φ_g| at z=±2.5cm for a 50kV asymmetric capacitor (γ=1, static):
  TTB:        Φ_g(+z, point)=1.541e4   Φ_g(−z, plate)=3.630e2   → 42.4× asymmetry, leans toward the POINT electrode.
  symmetric:  Φ_g(+z)=2.795e3 = Φ_g(−z)               → 1.00× (perfectly balanced control).
So the static γ-coupling makes the TTB a strongly DIRECTIONAL gravitational-scalar source (42×), biased toward the small/point electrode — matching the canonical Townsend-Brown thrust direction. Symmetric capacitor is balanced, confirming the asymmetry is geometry-driven, not numerical. This is the falsifiable bench prediction the user was after. Full suite 23 ok/0 fail.

title: EED time-domain FDTD is unconditionally unstable for γ≠0 (cross-coupling skew update → NaN)
description:
The potential-primary leapfrog (shaders/fdtd_em.wgsl, vel_step) blows up to all-NaN
for any γ>0 (i.e. the actual EED mode). Discovered while validating ORC-x7m: an AC
open helix at γ=1 produces a_vec = 89373/143748 NaN and c_fld = 35557/35937 NaN,
while γ=0 (Lorenz/Maxwell) is finite and correct.

ROOT CAUSE (proven analytically + empirically):
vel_step applies the EED gauge cross-coupling as
    phi_vel += dt·c²·(lap_phi − γ·div(a_vel_old))
    a_vel   += dt·c²·(lap_a   − γ·grad(phi_vel_old))
BOTH terms read the OLD velocities. For a longitudinal mode (β = dt·c²·γ·k) the
coupling sub-update is the skew matrix [[1,−iβ],[−iβ,1]], whose eigenvalues are
1∓iβ with |λ| = √(1+β²) > 1. So it grows every step for ANY dt>0 —
UNCONDITIONALLY unstable, not a CFL issue. Confirmed: reducing dt from CFL
(1.2e-11s) to 3e-12s left the NaN count identical; setting γ=0 made it finite.

FIX (Gauss-Seidel / symplectic ordering): update phi_vel first, then update a_vel
using the NEW phi_vel. That sub-update becomes [[1,−iβ],[−iβ,1−β²]] with det=1,
trace=2−β² → conditionally stable for β≤2 (a real CFL bound). On GPU this means
splitting vel_step into two sequential compute passes (vel_step_phi writes phi_vel;
vel_step_a reads the freshly-written phi_vel, writes a_vel) to avoid the
intra-pass write race. Apply to BOTH run_fdtd and run_fdtd_ac (and any sponge
variant). Then re-validate the γ=1 AC open helix stays finite and C≠0.
notes:
FIXED & VALIDATED. Three-part fix landed:

1. Gauss-Seidel pass split (shaders/fdtd_em.wgsl): vel_step replaced by vel_step_phi (writes phi_vel from div(a_vel@n)) then vel_step_a (reads the FRESH phi_vel for grad term). Sub-update becomes [[1,-iB],[-iB,1-B^2]], det=1, trace=2-B^2 -> conditionally stable for B<=2 instead of the old skew [[1,-iB],[-iB,1]] with |lambda|=sqrt(1+B^2)>1. On GPU done as two sequential compute passes to avoid the intra-pass neighbor-read race. Applied to run_fdtd_sponge AND run_fdtd_ac via shared fdtd_em_bgl/em_pl explicit BindGroupLayout+PipelineLayout (auto layout:None stripped unused bindings and mismatched across passes).

2. Spurious c^2 drop (A-equation): the grad(phi_vel) cross term had a c^2 factor it should not (physically c^2.grad(C) = c^2.grad(div A) + grad(dphi/dt); the dphi/dt piece carries NO c^2). That made B~5e8 at CFL -> still NaN even after the GS split. Line now reads C2*lap_ax - gamma*gpv_x (no C2 on the gamma term).

3. CFL safety factor 0.5 (lib.rs, both EM and GEM dt selection): bare wave leapfrog sits at dt.omega=2 (marginal) at exactly dx/(c.sqrt3); cross-coupling tips it over. dt sweep: 0.5.CFL stable, 0.75.CFL stable, 0.91.CFL NaN.

VALIDATION: AC open helix at gamma=1 now finite, C!=0 (|C|=1.74e-2). energy_conservation, c_field_wave, slw_propagation all still pass. gem_dynamic_c_coupling passes.

OPEN PHYSICS GAP (separate from stability, flagged to user): A-eq still MISSING the -c^2.grad(div A) portion of -c^2.grad(C); and the phi-equation form is non-standard. These are EED-model decisions for the user to own.
close_reason: Fixed and validated; full test suite green (14 integration files + doctests)

title: Rescale GEM internally so κ_G drops out of the equations (f32 precision)
description:
f32 cannot represent the real Kaluza-Klein κ_G (~7.4×10⁻²⁸) or even the Li-Torr value (~1.14×10⁻¹¹) without silent zero-rounding against the leading c²·∇²Φ_g term (c² ≈ 9×10¹⁶). Any multiplication of κ_G into the EoM is lost.

## Fix
Evolve **rescaled variables** Φ̃_g := Φ_g / κ_G and Ã_g := A_g / κ_G internally. The EoM then have O(1) coupling coefficients:
  ∂²Φ̃_g/∂t² = c²∇²Φ̃_g + (sources)/κ_G + C        ← κ_G factored out of the EED drive
  ∂²Ã_g/∂t² = c²∇²Ã_g + (sources)/κ_G + A         ← (per ORC-2's direct coupling)

At readback, multiply by κ_G to recover the physical-magnitude field.

## Notes
- Mass sources (ρ_m, J_m, when ORC-7 lands) must be pre-divided by κ_G before injection.
- Document the rescaling clearly at the top of fdtd_gem.wgsl — it's a footgun otherwise.
- Add a debug overlay showing the displayed-vs-physical magnitudes side-by-side.

## Depends on
ORC-2 (need direct coupling form before rescaling makes sense; rescaling derivative coupling is straightforward but less interesting).
notes:
DONE — but the bead's premise was a misdiagnosis, so the fix is f64 magnitude reduction, NOT internal EoM rescaling. Physical κ_G is now visible end-to-end (regression-tested).

## The bead's stated mechanism is wrong for our architecture
The bead says κ_G (~7.4e-28) is "lost against the leading c²·∇²Φ_g term (c²≈9e16)" in the EoM. Two reasons that does not apply:
1. ORC-bn6 made KK-direct a pointwise ALGEBRAIC assignment (A_g=κ_G·A, Φ_g=κ_G·C) — there is NO c²∇² term in that path to lose precision against.
2. Even for the SLW wave channel (fdtd_gem.wgsl), the GEM field is sourced ONLY by κ_G·∂C/∂t, so Φ_g itself is O(κ_G). Then c²∇²Φ_g and the κ_G·source term BOTH carry the κ_G factor — their ratio is κ_G-independent. There is no O(1)-vs-O(κ_G) cancellation for rescaling to cure. Dividing through by κ_G (Φ̃_g=Φ_g/κ_G) leaves the exact same internal ratio, so it would not have helped.

## The ACTUAL underflow (found empirically, tests/gem_kappa_precision.rs)
At physical κ_G the GEM *components* are fine in f32: a_g_vec=κ_G·a_src≈7.4e-28×1.16e-5≈8.6e-33 and b_g_vec≈9e-31 — both well above the f32 normal floor (1.18e-38). What underflowed was the MAGNITUDE REDUCTION |B_g|=sqrt(Σ cᵢ²) done in f32: squaring ~1e-30 gives ~1e-60, far below the f32 floor, so it flushed to 0 and the whole magnitude collapsed. (Classic f32 squaring-underflow; same signature as the energy-density case.)

## Fix (solver-gpu/src/postproc/mod.rs)
New helper vec3_mag_f64(): accumulates the squared sum in f64 (floor ~2e-308) and casts the result back to f32. Wired into all three vector-magnitude reduction sites: compute_maxima::vec_max, extract_slice::slice_magnitude, extract_volume (B/A/B_g arms). Channel-agnostic — fixes KK-direct, SLW, and Li-Torr magnitudes equally. No buffer rescaling, no κ_G threading.

## Why NOT buffer rescaling (the bead's proposed fix)
Li-Torr writes a PHYSICAL-unit A_g (the −(mₑ/e)ω×r London moment, independent of κ_G) into the SAME a_g_vec buffer that KK/SLW write. A κ_G readback-rescale would corrupt Li-Torr. Rescaling also adds a documented footgun for zero benefit over the f64 reduction.

## Validation (tests/gem_kappa_precision.rs, PASSES)
DC toroid, KK-direct, 32³:
  |B_g| (κ_G=1)        = 1.2177e-3 1/s
  |B_g| (κ_G=7.4e-28)  = 9.0110e-31 1/s   (was 0.0 before the fix)
  ratio                = 7.4000e-28  ==  κ_G exactly (linear, no precision loss)
Full solver-gpu suite green (14 binaries) — f64 reduction left every existing EM/GEM/Li-Torr magnitude assertion unchanged.

## Residual limit (documented, not a practical issue)
GPU f32 STORAGE of a_g_vec=κ_G·A still underflows if κ_G·A < 1.18e-38, i.e. |A| < 1.6e-11 for the KK κ_G. No realistic source reaches that (toroid |A|~1e-5). If a future ultra-weak-source regime needs it, per-channel rescaling (excluding Li-Torr) would be the escalation.

## Not done (optional, deferred)
The bead's "debug overlay showing displayed-vs-physical magnitudes side-by-side" — UI nicety, not needed for correctness; left for a frontend pass.

title: Interleave EM and GEM FDTD steps (real coupled evolution)
description:
## Problem
EM and GEM FDTDs run **sequentially**, not interleaved (lib.rs:266–281):
1. EM FDTD runs all n_steps.
2. `c_fld_prev` is snapshotted ONCE at the start of EM (state.rs:743).
3. `c_fld` is updated ONCE at the end of EM (state.rs:770–782).
4. GEM FDTD then runs separately, using these frozen snapshots.

Consequences:
- `∇C` seen by GEM is the post-EM steady-state gradient, constant across all GEM steps — no dynamics.
- `dC_dt` = (C_final − C_initial) / dt, where dt is one CFL step but the actual ΔC happened over n_steps·dt — **scale error of n_steps**.
- No back-reaction at all: A_g changes cannot drive A. (Even in the paper this is one-way at the linear level, but the EED-side ∇C dynamics during evolution are completely missed.)

## Fix
Move the GEM `vel_gem`/`pos_gem` dispatch *inside* the EM FDTD loop in `state.rs::run_fdtd_sponge` and `run_fdtd_ac`:

```
for each step:
    copy c_fld → c_fld_prev          // per-step snapshot
    vel_step (EM)
    pos_step (EM)
    update_c                          // C reflects new A and ∂φ/∂t
    if gem.enabled:
        vel_gem
        pos_gem
```

Per-step `c_fld_prev` snapshot makes `dC_dt = (C_new − C_old) / dt` numerically correct.

## Notes
- Combine both kernel suites into one command buffer per step batch (keep the 32-step Metal-watchdog batching).
- Drop the standalone `run_gem_fdtd` once integrated, or keep as a fallback for post-hoc forcing studies.

## Depends on
None — this is a pure correctness fix and benefits any coupling form. Can be done in parallel with ORC-2/3/4. But likely most visible AFTER ORC-2 (the SLW-mediated path is so weak per-step that the interleaving error may be invisible).

- New GemStepper (state.rs): builds vel_gem_phi/vel_gem_a/pos_gem pipelines + shared 7-binding bind group once; encode_step() dispatches the 3 passes into the EM command buffer.
- run_fdtd_sponge + run_fdtd_ac take Option<f32> gem_kappa. When Some: per EM step → copy c_fld→c_fld_prev, [inject], vel_phi/vel_a/pos, update_c, then GemStepper.encode_step. So ∂C/∂t=(C^{n+1}−C^n)/dt is exact and ∇C is live. When None: byte-identical to the old path (pre-loop copy once, post-loop update_c once) — all 11 non-GEM/static tests unchanged.

title: Add static-mode GEM solve (Poisson ∇²Φ_g = −κ_G·C)
description:
Static-mode solves currently skip GEM entirely (lib.rs:267 gates GEM on SolverMode::TimeDomain). But the paper's flagship configurations — toroid generating A in field-free region, Maxwell-Lodge effect, VPT — are inherently *static* or quasi-static. Time-domain is overkill (and slow) for those.

## Fix
After static EED solve completes (φ, A populated, C derived), if `gem.enabled` and we're in Static mode, run an elliptic solve:
  ∇²Φ_g = −κ_G · C        (Φ_g sourced by EED scalar directly, KK-direct form)
  ∇²A_g = −κ_G · A         (per-component, KK-direct A coupling)

Reuse the existing PCG scalar solver (`run_cg_phi`) — same Laplacian stencil, just different RHS. For A_g add a vector variant (three independent scalar CGs).

## Why this is high-value
The very first thing the user wants to see is: \"turn on a torus, do I see Φ_g track the A-field structure?\" Static mode gives that in <100 ms vs the seconds-to-minutes of an FDTD ramp-up. Makes the demo viscerally compelling.

## Depends on
ORC-2 (KK-direct coupling form) — the SLW-mediated derivative form has no static analog.

title: Implement Li-Torr gravitomagnetic London moment: B_g = −(2m_e/e)·ω
description:
The paper's most concrete, falsifiable electrogravitic prediction (Wilhelm 2026 Eq. 23) is **completely unwired**:

> A rotating superconductor sources a gravitomagnetic field B_g = −(2m_e/e)·ω where ω is the angular velocity of the condensate. Identical structure to the electromagnetic London moment, mass-to-charge ratio replacing the inverse.

## Current state
- `CoilEntity.superconducting: bool`  exists (types.rs:55) — read by zero kernels
- `GemParams.li_torr_mode: bool`      exists (types.rs:180) — read by zero kernels
- No angular-velocity field on any entity

## Fix
1. Add `angular_velocity_rad_s: [f64;3]` to CoilEntity (default zero, identity rotation axis).
2. New shader `shaders/li_torr_source.wgsl`: for each vertex inside the volume of a superconducting entity, **directly set** `b_g_vec[v] = -(2.0 * M_E / E) * omega`. This is a direct source, NOT a κ_G-mediated coupling — the Cooper-pair condensate physically fixes A_g in the London sense per the paper, no EED intermediary.
3. Dispatch after Biot-Savart in both static and time-domain modes.
4. Constant: 2·m_e/e = 1.1374×10⁻¹¹ (use f32 literal; magnitude is large enough to survive f32).
5. UI: angular velocity input on entity panel (rad/s, three axes), gated behind `superconducting=true`.

## Validation test
Sphere entity, superconducting=true, ω = [0, 0, 100] rad/s. Expected: |B_g| ≈ 1.14×10⁻⁹ uniformly inside the sphere, zero outside. Compare against analytic.

## Why P0
This is the *one* paper prediction that doesn't depend on speculative κ_G magnitudes — the coupling constant 2m_e/e is fixed by known particle physics. If the sim can't reproduce Eq. 23, it can't claim to test EED predictions at all.

## Independent of
ORC-2 and ORC-3 (this is direct entity-sourced, not C-mediated).
notes:
## Implemented

**Backend (solver-gpu):**
- `CoilEntity.angular_velocity_rad_s: [f64;3]` (serde-default zero, so existing data deserializes unchanged)
- `shaders/li_torr_source.wgsl` — algebraic A_g(r) = −(m_e/e)·(ω×(r−r_c)) inside SC sphere (radius = coil.radius_m). Overwrites A_g inside SC volumes only; leaves the rest of the field untouched so future κ_G superposition works.
- `shaders/derive_gem.wgsl` — B_g = ∇×A_g (central difference, mirrors derive.wgsl).
- `GpuGridState.b_g_vec` buffer + `LiTorrEntityGpu` (packed as 2×vec4 to dodge WGSL vec3 alignment).
- `run_li_torr_source` and `run_derive_gem_fields` dispatch methods.
- Pipeline wired in `OracleSolver::solve`: when `gem.enabled && gem.li_torr_mode`, filter entities by `superconducting && |ω|>0`, dispatch Li-Torr, then derive B_g. Works in **both static and time-domain modes** (Li-Torr is direct sourcing, not C-mediated).
- Warning if `li_torr_mode=true` but no qualifying entity.
- `BgMagnitude` wired in postproc: slice extraction, volume extraction, maxima — previously fell through to a zero-fill.

**Frontend (TypeScript):**
- `CoilEntity.angular_velocity_rad_s?: [number,number,number]` (optional — default omits, treated as zero by serde-default).

title: Inject ρ (charge accumulation at open-circuit tips) to source the temporal half of C
description:
The FDTD injects only J (into the A-equation, inject_j.wgsl); ρ is never injected. Consequence: the EED scalar C = (1/c²)∂ₜφ + ∇·A only gets its spatial half (∇·A, sourced by ∇·J at the tips). The temporal half (1/c²)∂ₜφ requires φ to be sourced, which physically comes from charge accumulation ∂ₜρ = −∇·J at the open-circuit tips of the helix.

This matters most under a DECOUPLED potential evolution (□φ=ρ/ε₀, □A=µ₀J): with no ρ source and no φ↔A cross-coupling, φ≡0 identically, so C collapses to ∇·A alone and the (1/c²)∂ₜφ contribution to Φ_g vanishes. Under the current cross-coupled form, φ is instead driven by the −c²∂ₜ(∇·A) proxy term — which is the (unstable, KK-inconsistent) substitute for real ρ injection.

CAUTION: naive ρ injection via exact continuity (∂ₜρ=−∇·J) makes ∂µJµ=0 → □C=0 → C never sources at all. The open-helix EED prediction REQUIRES ∂µJµ≠0. So this needs the deliberate idealization: prescribe J as a current-source BC at the tips WITHOUT the compensating ρ (or with a partial ρ), keeping ∂µJµ≠0. Decide the exact model when picking this up. Blocked on the coupling-vs-decoupling theory decision.
notes: Theory decision RESOLVED 2026-05-29: project committed to the coupled propagating EED form (see FIELD_THEORY.md). So this is no longer blocked on that fork. Remaining design question stands: prescribe J as a current-source BC at the tips keeping ∂µJµ≠0 (do NOT impose exact continuity ∂ₜρ=−∇·J, which would zero ∂µJµ and kill C). This would add the physically-real source for C's temporal (1/c²)∂ₜφ half (currently only generated indirectly via the γ cross-coupling).
